title: A Garden Grows
passages: Maya had a small patch of dirt behind her house and a paper envelope holding twenty seeds. She sorted them on the kitchen table: eight bean seeds, seven squash seeds, and five tiny carrot seeds that looked like crumbs. Her neighbor, Mr. Okafor, leaned over the fence to watch. He told her that in the mountain village where he grew up, families sang a short song to each new row so the plants would feel welcome. Maya liked that idea very much. She dug shallow holes, dropped in each seed, and hummed a tune she made up herself. Then she watered every row with METICULOUS care.

For six days, nothing happened, and Maya checked the soil every morning before breakfast. On the seventh day, a pale green shoot pushed up through the dirt. By day twelve, fourteen of her twenty seeds had begun to GERMINATE. The bean plants sent curly TENDRILS climbing up the sticks she had planted beside them. Mr. Okafor said his grandmother used to tie bright ribbons to the tallest stalks, and Maya wondered what other gardeners around the world did for luck. After forty days, her little patch was ABUNDANT with leaves, blossoms, and one very proud squash.
